name: Baron René de Mackau

summary.text: Ange René Armand, baron de Mackau, a French naval captain and gentleman of the king's chamber, was sent in 1825 to carry Charles X's ordinance of 17 April 1825 to Haiti. The ordinance recognised Haitian independence on condition of a 150-million-franc indemnity payable in five annual instalments and halved customs duties for French ships. Mackau arrived at Port-au-Prince on 3 July 1825 with a squadron of warships and instructions to obtain President Boyer's agreement, by constraint if necessary; Boyer accepted and the Haitian Senate ratified the ordinance on 11 July 1825. Mackau's report on the mission was written later that year.

facts.claim: Charles X's ordinance of 17 April 1825 recognised the independence of the former colony of Saint-Domingue on condition that the Republic of Haiti pay 150 million gold francs to indemnify French colonists who had fled the colony between 1791 and 1804.
facts.quote: Cette reconnaissance était soumise au paiement, par la république d'Haïti, d'une somme de 150 millions de francs-or destinée à indemniser les colons français

facts.claim: The ordinance was entrusted to the baron de Mackau, gentleman of the king's chamber and naval captain, to carry to Boyer and propose that he accept it.
facts.quote: gentilhomme de la chambre du roi et capitaine de vaisseau, pour la porter à Boyer et lui proposer de l'accepter

facts.claim: On 3 July 1825 fourteen warships armed with 528 cannon arrived in the roads of Port-au-Prince; accounts differ on the composition of the squadron, one giving seven corvettes and twelve ships.
facts.quote: le 3 juillet 1825, 14 navires de guerres armés de 528 canons arrivent dans la rade de Port-au-Prince

facts.claim: Mackau's instructions were to obtain Boyer's agreement including by constraint; he threatened to use force if President Boyer and the Haitian Senate refused the ordinance's terms.
facts.quote: Mackau avait pour instruction d'obtenir l'accord de Boyer y compris par la contrainte

facts.claim: The Haitian commissioners objected to the form of the ordinance; Boyer held two conferences with the armed negotiator and wrote on 11 July that he accepted the text, promising to have it ratified by the Senate, which did so on 11 July 1825. One source gives 8 July for Boyer's acceptance.
facts.quote: Boyer a écrit le 11 juillet qu'il acceptait le texte

facts.claim: Under the ordinance the indemnity was payable in five annual instalments of 30 million francs, the first in December 1825, and customs duties on French ships and goods were reduced by half; the indemnity was reduced to 90 million francs in 1838 under Louis-Philippe.
facts.quote: the Haitian state was to pay the sum in five annual instalments of 30 million francs, the first in December 1825

facts.claim: On his return Mackau wrote a report on the mission, dated August 1825 by one account and September 1825 by another; it has been published in a collective volume, 'Haïti-France, les chaînes de la dette. Le rapport Mackau (1825)'.

openQuestions: Site claim tested: 'A French squadron of 14 warships under Baron de Mackau backed the 1825 demand' — supported (14 warships, 528 cannon, 3 July 1825), though one account gives a different composition.
Site claim tested: the 150-million-franc indemnity conditional on recognition — supported.

The Gallica originals (the ordinance and Mackau's report) were not returned by the searches; the Wikisource text of Ardouin's Études and the collective volume on the Mackau report are the closest to primary sources opened.
Site claim that the last payments on refinanced debt were not made until 1947 was not researched here.
